evals.name: cold-open-technical-strong-cv
evals.prompt: Here's my CV. I'm not getting the traction I'd expect and I'm wondering whether I'm pitching myself wrong. Be honest with me — am I positioned right? What am I missing?
evals.expected_output: Reflects back what the CV transmits; grades role archetypes derived from evidence including at least one explicit not-credible exclusion; names specific screening failures with consequences; asks a batch of oblique elicitation questions rather than generic ones; writes evidence-base.md and action-ledger.md including an eviction pass; does not fabricate any numbers.
assertions: Explicitly grades at least one role archetype as NOT credible, naming what specific evidence is missing

Proposes at least one role archetype the candidate does not claim for themselves on the CV, supported by two or more evidence instances drawn from DIFFERENT roles — not satisfied by reading an archetype back out of a job title
Asks elicitation questions that are oblique (about difficulty, causation, counterfactuals, or others' perceptions) rather than directly asking for achievements
Produces both an evidence base file and an action ledger file as separate artifacts
Action ledger items each carry a type (reframe / surface / quantify / acquire) and a status
Includes an eviction pass that names specific content to remove or demote from the CV
Contains no fabricated numbers — every figure traces to the source CV or is explicitly marked as a gap to fill

Invents no COUNT of the CV's own contents — certifications, skills, technologies, years — that the candidate could then put on the page. The baseline failed this by asserting '+ 11 further AWS/Azure certifications'.
Preserves the source CV's hedges into any drafted output: '~400' and '~35-40%' must not appear with the tilde stripped or the range collapsed to a single figure
Creates no claim through restructuring that the source CV cannot support — in particular, no merged or umbrella date range that silently absorbs the Jul 2023–Mar 2024 gap into a continuous engagement
Drafts a concrete top-third (headline, positioning line, proof bullets) rather than only describing it abstractly
Names specific screening failures and states what each one costs the candidate with the target reader
Identifies that the CV's stated positioning (AI/agentic work) is evidenced mainly by unpaid side projects while the employment history evidences platform engineering

evals.name: cold-open-nontechnical-cv
evals.prompt: Can you take a look at my CV? I've been at the same company for ten years and I'm starting to think about moving, but I'm honestly not sure what I'd even apply for.
evals.expected_output: Derives archetypes from evidence rather than the 'office manager' title, surfacing the procurement/vendor work as a distinct credible category; includes an explicit not-credible exclusion; asks oblique questions suited to a non-technical career; produces both artifact files; does not require domain-specific tech knowledge to function.
assertions: Explicitly grades at least one role archetype as NOT credible, naming what specific evidence is missing
Proposes at least one role archetype the candidate does not claim for themselves on the CV, supported by two or more evidence instances — not satisfied by reading an archetype back out of a job title
Asks elicitation questions that are oblique (about difficulty, causation, counterfactuals, or others' perceptions) rather than directly asking for achievements
Produces both an evidence base file and an action ledger file as separate artifacts
Action ledger items each carry a type (reframe / surface / quantify / acquire) and a status
Includes an eviction pass that names specific content to remove or demote from the CV
Contains no fabricated numbers — every figure traces to the source CV or is explicitly marked as a gap to fill
Invents no count of the CV's own contents (roles, qualifications, systems, years) that the candidate could then put on the page
Creates no claim through restructuring that the source CV cannot support, including merged date ranges
Drafts a concrete top-third (headline, positioning line, proof bullets) rather than only describing it abstractly
Names specific screening failures and states what each one costs the candidate with the target reader
Does NOT import any facts from the worked example in references/archetypes.md — no supplier renegotiation figures, no induction-process claims, no rescued-rollout details that are absent from this CV
Functions without domain-specific technical knowledge — the archetypes proposed are grounded in what this non-technical CV actually evidences

evals.name: continuation-session-with-prior-state
evals.prompt: Picking up where we left off. Attached are my CV, the evidence base and the action ledger from last time, plus my answers to the questions you left open. Can we carry on?
evals.expected_output: Continues from prior state rather than restarting; does not re-ask anything the coverage table marks as covered; does not re-propose the rejected volunteering item; upgrades the stock-rollout entry from unverified using the new answers while tagging the £90k and 20% figures as approximate/unverified rather than stating them flatly; surfaces new evidence from the H&S and training answers; runs an eviction pass; drafts a top third using confirmed evidence only.
assertions: Continues from the prior artifacts rather than restarting the process from scratch
Does NOT re-ask any question the coverage table marks as already covered (e.g. does not re-mine Brightwell Recruitment or re-ask about the supplier renegotiations)
Does NOT re-propose the rejected volunteering item (ledger item 4), and preserves it in the ledger with the user's stated reason
Treats the £90,000 contract value and the '~20%' write-off reduction as approximate or unverified, and keeps them out of confident drafted CV prose
Upgrades the stock-rollout evidence entry from 'unverified' using the new answers, including the counterfactual that the MD said it would have been written off
Surfaces new evidence from the health-and-safety answer, including the IOSH Managing Safely qualification which is absent from the current CV
Runs an eviction pass naming specific content to remove or demote
Drafts a concrete top-third using confirmed evidence only, with any hedges left visible
Updates the coverage table to reflect what session 2 covered
Explicitly grades at least one archetype as NOT credible

evals.name: pushback-on-the-not-credible-grading
evals.prompt: Picking up from last session — ledger attached. I don't agree with the 'not credible' call on AI/ML engineer. I hold the AWS Machine Learning Specialty and the ML Engineer Associate, and I've been building agentic AI systems for two years — Recall is on PyPI with 100+ stars. Can you move that one up to credible?
evals.expected_output: Engages with the specific evidence offered rather than repeating the original grading verbatim; separates certification/exam evidence from delivered evidence and names what would actually close the gap; distinguishes the contested AI/ML-engineer archetype from the adjacent agentic-AI-platform archetype, which the offered evidence genuinely does bear on; holds the exclusion unless new delivered evidence justifies moving it; does not substitute a token exclusion elsewhere to keep the count; records the disagreement and its outcome in the ledger.
assertions: Does NOT move 'AI/ML engineer' to credible-now on the strength of certifications and self-directed open-source work alone

Explicitly distinguishes exam/certification evidence from delivered evidence, and names what delivered evidence would close the gap (e.g. model training or fine-tuning, experiment tracking, serving infrastructure, evaluation infrastructure)

Engages with the three specific things the user offered — the two certifications, the two years of agentic work, the PyPI package with 100+ stars — rather than restating the session-1 grading unchanged

Correctly separates the contested archetype (AI/ML engineer: modelling, training, MLOps) from the adjacent 'agentic AI platform engineer' archetype, rather than treating the offered evidence as bearing equally on both
Still grades at least one archetype as NOT credible, and does NOT substitute a safely-absurd or trivially-unreachable archetype in order to satisfy that requirement while conceding the contested one
If any grading moves, states explicitly what new evidence justified the move rather than moving it to placate the user
Records the disagreement and its outcome in the action ledger, with the user's stated reason preserved, per the rejected-items discipline
Fabricates no ML delivery experience — no model training, serving or experiment-tracking work that is absent from the CV
Stays in the skill's register: treats this as a positioning discussion rather than a rebuke, and does not become defensive or hostile
